subject: Issues running SPDE models more than once with Microsoft Visual C++ error

messages.author: c7c5c2402e94537c
messages.subject: Issues running SPDE models more than once with Microsoft Visual C++ error
parts:
Hello,

I'm working on a project looking at mosquito abundance in Greece. For this I have point locations of mosquito traps and have been running an SPDE model with the formulation below:

form <- y ~ 0 + b0 + f(s, model = spde1)

mod1 <- inla(form,
             family = "poisson",
             data = inla.stack.data(stack.out),
             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE,
                                      A = inla.stack.A(stack.out)),
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE))

If I run it a first time after opening a session it usually runs fine. But if I try to rerun it, with or without changing parameters, then it won't run and I get the error box in the image. I then have to close R and restart the session if I want to modify the model (such as changing the family type or adding variables).  This box is then followed by the error message in the console below:
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully. If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>. *** inla.core.safe: inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=1/2 Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully. If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>. *** inla.core.safe: inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=2/2 *** inla.core.safe: rerun with improved initial values Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully. If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

What could cause this? Is this a RAM issue?

Thank you and best regards,
Jerome
